findings.title: Native add-on timeout cannot interrupt a stalled read
findings.why_it_matters: A session load can remain pending indefinitely when the underlying file read stalls, so the 120-second native timeout never reaches the official JavaScript fallback and application shutdown can also wait forever. The timer only sets a cancellation flag, while the add-on awaits the native task and the synchronous Rust read observes cancellation only after the blocking read returns. Running this read through the already killable helper-process boundary, or otherwise adding a hard completion bound outside the in-process native task, makes timeout and shutdown behavior enforceable.
findings.suggested_fix: Route native zstd reads through the NativeClient helper subprocess (whose timeout kills the process), or add an equivalent isolated boundary that can be forcibly terminated; ensure request() rejects at timeout and close() has a bounded wait, then verify official fallback after a deliberately stalled read.
evidence: desktop/native/addon.mjs:22-30 -- the timeout calls reader.close(), but execution then remains at `await pending` until the native promise settles.
desktop/native/addon.mjs:45-49 -- cleanup awaits the same pending task, and close() awaits all running reads without a second timeout.

native-addon/src/lib.rs:54-73 and native-helper/src/reader.rs:66-96 -- close only sets an AtomicBool; cancellation is checked between decode iterations, while `decoder.read(...)` is a synchronous filesystem read that must return before the flag is observed.

residual_risks: Successful loaded-image replacement retains `.before-native-*` sibling binaries with no cleanup path; this is bounded per deployment but can accumulate across repeated upgrades.

Rollback trusts any manifest located beneath install/repair-checks; an accidentally selected or locally modified manifest can operate on allowed install/plugin targets, although hash checks limit ordinary stale-manifest damage.
testing_gaps: No fault-injection test holds a native add-on read pending past timeout and proves request rejection, official fallback, and bounded AddonReadTransport.close().
Deployment tests cover journal states before and after mutation, but not process interruption during loaded-image rename/replacement followed by rollback and retained-image cleanup.
